newsitem.title: UK: UK financial services to spend more on IT in 1997.
newsitem.headline: UK financial services to spend more on IT in 1997.

text.p: Information technology investment is expected to grow strongly in 1997 with firms' intentions the most positive since early 1995, a survey by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and Coopers & Lybrand showed.

The fourth quarter survey of financial services showed capital spending on IT in the next 12 months -- including software, hardware, personnel and any other expenses related to IT -- would significantly increase.
"There will be much more of a focus on IT investment this year," Coopers & Lybrand partner Pat Newberry said.

He said IT investment was driven by a range of needs including handling multiple distribution channels, continuing to improve the efficiency and quality of service and dealing with forthcoming issues such as the year 2000 and the Euro.
He said British banks were working hard towards the proposed advent of the Euro, scheduled for January 1999.
"It will cost banks hundreds of millions," he said.
"The Euro is one of the biggest causes of expenditure that banks have seen for many years but it need not be a headache, it could be a great opportunity."
